narrative.northStar: The White Wall and the Blue Pane
narrative.overview: **Creative North Star: "The White Wall and the Blue Pane"** Every Israeli volunteer knows the apartment stairwell: a white rendered wall above, an oil-painted band below, cats asleep on the steps. This system keeps the wall white and puts every control in one deep slate blue; the navigation is that blue turned into a floating pane of tinted glass, so the map and the feed stay visible through it. The look is quiet on purpose. The volunteer is outdoors, in glare, one-handed, often at dusk, with a bowl in the other hand. Markers are the loudest thing on any screen; chrome never competes with them. The system is Operate-first: plain controls, 48 px targets, a real type scale, state shown as colour **and** an icon **and** a word. It borrows from the stairwell only a palette (white, one slate blue), a density, and one signature move (the glass pane). Navigation, forms and lists stay the standard ones a member already knows. The landing page is the one place the painted band appears as a full-width section, where it frames the sign-in button.
keyCharacteristics: White ground, one slate blue for everything tappable; the blue never appears on anything that is not a control or a selection.
Five state colours, never alone: each always has an icon and a word (green fine, orange running low, red needed, grey no data, plum for a cat alert).
Hebrew first and right to left; all layout in logical properties; the map canvas stays left to right because geography does not mirror.
The phone's own system sans: no font download, no third-party request.
Flat surfaces with 1 px lines; depth only for what floats (the lift) and the glass.

rules.name: The Tap Rule
rules.body: Slate blue means "you can tap this" or "this is chosen". Nothing else is that blue.

rules.name: The Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: A state colour is always paired with an icon and a word. A pin's colour is repeated by a corner mark (tick, clock, exclamation, dash); a chip carries its icon and label.

rules.name: The One Plum Rule
rules.body: Plum is reserved for cat alerts so that an alert can never be mistaken for a spot.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Times, counts and distances use tabular figures so a column of "last log 14 h ago" lines up.

rules.name: The Isolate Rule
rules.body: A name or a Latin word typed by a person sits in `<bdi>` (or an isolated value) inside Hebrew text so its punctuation cannot jump across the sentence.

rules.name: The Float-Only Rule
rules.body: Depth means "this sits over the content". A resting card never has a shadow.

rules.name: The Legible Glass Rule
rules.body: The glass is see-through, but the backdrop is dimmed before the tint is laid on, so its labels (#eef3fa, white when active) keep at least 4.5:1 even over a plain white page (5.3:1 for the inactive labels and 4.6:1 for the active one over plain white; the active tab is also bolder, not only lighter). If it is made clearer, dim the backdrop more; never trade away the contrast.

dos: **Do** keep slate blue for things that can be tapped or chosen (The Tap Rule).
**Do** pair every state colour with an icon and a word, in chips and notices (map pins are the one exception: the card and the legend carry the words).
**Do** use gender-neutral Hebrew: nouns, infinitives and plurals, never a "you" verb.
**Do** write errors as what happened and what to do next, in one or two plain sentences.
**Do** keep targets at 48 px or more (44 px for small buttons) and primary actions on the pinned bar, inside the thumb's reach.
**Do** let the glass fall back to solid when blur is off or transparency is reduced.
**Do** run every string through `t('key')` and every style through a class or a `data-*` attribute; no inline styles.

**Do** name every photo link and photo button by the photo's own name, and every icon-only control by what it does; a map marker is named by the spot and its state, and the member's position by "your location".
**Do** keep the focus ring white on slate (the bars, the landing band, the footer, the full-screen photo) and blue on white, at least 3:1 against what is behind it.
**Do** make a three-dots menu a disclosure (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`), not `role="menu"`, and name a dialog by its purpose ("Message actions"), not by the first line inside it.

**Do** give a selected or pressed state more than a fill or a shadow, so forced-colours mode shows it (an outline), and give every pane of glass a solid fallback for no blur and for reduced transparency.
**Do** set the page title to the screen's title, so a tab or a history list names it.
donts: **Don't** use cream, terracotta, neon-on-dark or a gamified look (badges, streaks, levels). Stats carry no prize.
**Don't** use a state colour on its own (except the colour of a map pin), or plum for anything but a cat alert.
**Don't** show the distance to a spot or the result of the location check beyond "counted" or "saved as unverified".
**Don't** put cat photos or any user photo on the map itself (pins, layers). The card that opens from a spot may show its most liked approved cat photo (Q37).
**Don't** add a coloured side stripe to a card or notice, a gradient text, or a shadow on a resting card.
**Don't** load a web font or a third-party script for chrome.
**Don't** let the glass fall below 4.5:1 for its labels (dim the backdrop rather than raise the tint), or put text smaller than 14 px on it.
